raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Accelerate long text prefills in DeepSeek V4's C128 attention on Hopper by processing eight neighboring queries together. Preserve the pinned FlashMLA accumulation and rounding order with unnormalized FP32 intermediate state. ## Claims - Speed up the C128 attention operation by **1.39× at 64k**, **2.05× at 128k**, and **5.27× at 1M** on H200 with 8,192 query tokens, including query packing and intermediate-buffer allocation. - Increase measured end-to-end total token throughput by **33.69% at 1M context** on `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp` at TP8/concurrency 1, with TTFT reduced by **25.43%**, using identical serving parameters. - Match the original FlashMLA BF16 output bits on the tested synthetic cases and sampled real-model C128 outputs. This is an operator-level result; it does not establish whole-model batch invariance or general task accuracy. - Automatically select the optimization for eligible SM90 text prefills with eight local heads, at least 512 compressed rows, and at least 4,096 query tokens. Other inputs continue through the existing FlashMLA path. ## Validation Context lengths use **k** and **M**: **1k = 1024 tokens**, **1M = 1024 × 1k**. Reproduction commands retain the integer token counts required by the CLI. Measured on 2026-10-26, using 8 × H200 (141 GB), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, and CUDA toolkit 13.2.78. Baseline source is unmodified `b689feb9f22129cb9ba65ea72e3e67e4a9c95355`; the candidate adds this C128 implementation. Both reuse the same installed non-C128 native libraries. FlashMLA is pinned to `e2afa5fd8c220fbd05fe03fc24c9d5e64c24641b`. **Operator benchmark.** BF16 Q/KV, head dimension 512, eight active heads in the existing 64-head layout, 8,192 query tokens. The optimized measurement includes the Python wrapper, Triton query packing, allocations, and both CUDA launches. The reference uses prebuilt sparse indices; excluding their construction favors the reference. Each point uses `triton.testing.do_bench(warmup=100, rep=300)`. | Context | FlashMLA (ms) | C128 (ms) | Speedup | Latency reduction | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 64k | 1.264 | 0.909 | 1.39× | 28.11% | | 128k | 2.077 | 1.015 | 2.05× | 51.12% | | 256k | 3.701 | 1.221 | 3.03× | 67.00% | | 512k | 7.045 | 1.687 | 4.18× | 76.06% | | 1M | 13.804 | 2.619 | 5.27× | 81.03% | All measured active output elements match bitwise. At the 4,096-query dispatch boundary, speedups are 1.38× / 2.01× / 5.22× at 64k / 128k / 1M. The operator table starts at 64k, matching the production context threshold; shorter contexts keep the original FlashMLA path. Latency reduction is `(FlashMLA - C128) / FlashMLA`. **Serving benchmark.** Checkpoint: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp`, architecture `DeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration`, text requests only. Both arms use TP8, FP8 KV, block size 256, 8,192 batched tokens, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`, `max_num_seqs=48`, chunked prefill, prefix caching, and **`indexer_tp_shard_min_rows=1`**. No parameter adjustment is counted as a code speedup. Each request has `context - 128` input tokens and exactly 128 generated tokens; concurrency 1, request rate `inf`, greedy sampling, and EOS ignored. Before each round, reset prefix caching. Each length has a separate one-request warmup. Report the median of three four-request rounds at 16k/128k/256k/512k and one four-request round at 1M. Both arms use seeds 20261024–20261026 for formal rounds and 8675309 for warmup. Serving measurements combine the original 16k/1M results, separate 128k baseline/candidate follow-ups, and the new 256k/512k comparisons. Original 128k results are retained below: | Context | Baseline total tok/s | C128 total tok/s | Change | Baseline TTFT (s) | C128 TTFT (s) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 128k | 26,972.88 | 27,641.20 | +2.48% | 4.137 | 4.023 | | 256k | 26,865.01 | 29,298.83 | +9.06% | 9.076 | 8.257 | | 512k | 23,902.60 | 28,424.22 | +18.92% | 21.325 | 17.827 | | 1M | 18,426.02 | 24,633.28 | +33.69% | 56.455 | 42.097 | Across the selected context rows, each arm completed **52/52 formal requests and 5/5 warmups**, without request errors or length mismatches. The 1M result is one round of four requests, not a multi-round confidence interval. Both arms use the existing legal threshold 1. At TP8, thresholds 1 give the same effective minimum of eight rows through `max(min_rows, tp_size)`; changing this parameter is not counted as a C128 code gain. Default-threshold results are recorded separately. 128k provides less opportunity than 1M: existing real-model records show 9 eligible C128 query chunks (180 calls per rank) versus 121 (2,420 calls). At the end-context microbenchmark, each call saves about 1.06 ms at 128k versus 11.19 ms at 1M. Even estimating all 180 calls at the larger 128k endpoint saving yields only about 191 ms against approximately four seconds TTFT; this is an illustrative estimate, not a profiler breakdown. Other layers, indexer work, communication, and decode limit the end-to-end benefit. The additional 256k/512k runs completed 24/24 formal requests and 2/2 warmups per arm, with throughput changes of **+9.06% / +18.92%**. Both arms kept the same serving flags and seeds. One interrupted benchmark attempt is preserved separately; the table reports the complete rerun. **Correctness and execution checks.** - `127 passed in 19.93s` for `test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` and the unchanged `test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py`. The C128 tests directly exercise the native operation and compare active BF16 bits against FlashMLA, including compressed/SWA boundaries, partial query groups, offsets, NaN padding, sink cases, and unchanged output padding. - On real model inputs, sampled the first and last 17 queries of every eligible C128 call across all eight ranks: **20,800 calls, 2,896,691,200 BF16 elements, zero bit mismatches**. Contexts range from 64k to approximately 1023.54k; the final partial prefill chunk is included. Intermediate query rows are not exhaustively checked. - The original and optimized services both returned the expected access code at 16k, 128k, and 1M. All three generated token sequences and top-1 selections matched. Maximum generated-token logprob differences by length were 5.96046e-07 / 4.41072e-06 / 0.000900202. This is a three-case retrieval smoke evaluation, not a broad accuracy benchmark. - Incremental C++/SM90a CUDA build passed. The existing H100 Attention CI task selects the attention test directory, with source dependencies extended to include the new model operation, native sources, and FlashMLA build file. Checkpoint serving and retrieval validation were run outside CI; the local vision checkpoint and eight-GPU serving setup are not provided by that CI task. - Applicable pre-commit hooks passed: Ruff, formatting, mypy, clang-format, Markdown, SPDX, and test tethering. This records local validation, not an upstream CI result.
Reproduction commands Build the candidate's `_c128_C` target using the repository's incremental CMake workflow, with SM90a enabled. Run these commands from the candidate checkout: ```bash PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py -q PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python \ benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_deepseek_v4_c128_prefill.py \ --contexts 65536 131072 262144 524288 1048576 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python \ benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_deepseek_v4_c128_prefill.py \ --query-len 4096 --contexts 65536 131072 1048576 ``` For end-to-end results, start a clean baseline checkout and the candidate separately with the same checkpoint and command. `$MODEL` is the path to `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp`. ```bash export PYTHONPATH="$PWD" export VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 # Allows prefix-cache resets between rounds. .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL" \ --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --max-num-seqs 48 --max-model-len auto \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-chunked-prefill \ --safetensors-load-strategy=prefetch --enable-prefix-caching \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --served-model-name dsv4-flash-vision \ --attention-config '{"indexer_tp_shard_min_rows":1}' ``` For each context length, reset caching, run one warmup, then reset caching before each formal round. Set `CONTEXT_K` to 16 / 128 / 256 / 512 / 1024 and `CONTEXT=$((CONTEXT_K * 1024))`, `NUM_PROMPTS=1` and `SEED=8675309` for warmup, then `NUM_PROMPTS=4` and the formal round's seed. ```bash curl --fail -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8001/reset_prefix_cache .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \ --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8001 \ --model dsv4-flash-vision --tokenizer "$MODEL" \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len "$((CONTEXT - 128))" \ --random-output-len 128 --random-range-ratio 0 --random-prefix-len 0 \ --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" --max-concurrency 1 --request-rate inf \ --seed "$SEED" --ignore-eos --num-warmups 0 \ --ready-check-timeout-sec 0 --extra-body '{"temperature":0}' \ --save-result --save-detailed --result-dir "$RESULT_DIR" \ --result-filename "$RESULT_FILE" ``` Serving measurements use the regular CLI without reference-comparison instrumentation. Full-service `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` stopped in the unchanged vision embedding CPU-to-GPU copy before C128. A separate validation service applies the same sync checker only around C128 and compares the first/last 17 query tokens of every eligible C128 call against FlashMLA across all eight ranks. Only evaluation-side comparisons are inside `gpu_sync_allowed()`; the production C128 call remains outside it.
## Details The original Hopper sparse prefill processes each query with 64 head rows, although this TP8 workload has only eight active heads. Neighboring queries in C128 layers attend to almost the same long, contiguous compressed prefix. Packing eight queries × eight heads fills those 64 rows with useful work and shares prefix KV loads. A Triton helper packs Q. A native CUDA shared-prefix kernel computes complete common prefix tiles and saves the unnormalized FP32 output accumulator, maximum, and unreduced denominator state. A second CUDA kernel resumes each query's remaining compressed tiles and sliding window, applies its attention sink, and normalizes once. Keeping this raw state preserves the reference's reduction and rounding sequence; normalizing and reconstructing prefix state would introduce BF16 differences. The attention computation uses CUDA; there is no Triton attention fallback. Dispatch stays inside the existing DeepSeek V4 NVIDIA attention implementation. It requires the native extension, SM90, BF16 Q, compression ratio 128, eight local heads, a 128-token window, no extended image visibility, non-batch-invariant execution, one prefill request in the workspace group, at least 512 compressed rows, and at least 4,096 queries. The compressed-row threshold corresponds to approximately 64k original context tokens. It is checked per workspace group and query chunk, rather than against global client concurrency. The change does not modify scheduler, model-runner, KV-cache manager, indexer configuration, or decode logic. It continues using the existing BF16 KV gather. `_c128_C` is an optional SM90a extension built alongside FlashMLA; installations without it use the original path. The vendored adaptation retains the upstream FlashMLA MIT notice and identifies the source version. **Tradeoffs and limits.** Packing and the separate tail kernel add overhead, motivating the dispatch thresholds. Staging uses 203,689,984 bytes (194.25 MiB) per rank at 8,192 query tokens, and scales with query count. The existing dummy profiling path does not explicitly allocate this added staging. The tested 8,192-token configuration completed long-context serving; this does not validate memory budgeting at 32k batched tokens or at higher concurrency. Multi-image requests, other head counts, other architectures, decode speed, and full model quality benchmarks are outside the measured claims. Exact output agreement is scoped to the tested Hopper implementation and pinned dependency/compiler versions.
Related work and duplicate check (2026-10-26) Query grouping is an existing optimization direction. [vLLM #48726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48726) includes structure-aware C128 query packing on SM100 alongside indexer optimizations. This change targets SM90, uses BF16 gathered KV, and preserves legacy FlashMLA arithmetic through explicit prefix-state continuation. [#63104](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63104) groups queries for FA4 sparse prefill with 16–64 local heads on SM100. [SGLang #32779](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32779) uses Triton sparse-query unions, including on SM90, rather than this native C128 continuation. [#59131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59131) reuses gathered KV across layers; [#41836](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41836) avoids BF16 gathering via a KV-cache path. This implementation retains gathering and shares KV within a query tile. [FlashMLA #170](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA/pull/170) changes producer scheduling; [FlashMLA #227](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA/pull/227) targets fused H64 attention on B200. The base already includes [#61615](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61615), enabling the existing small-head operation for V4.1. That per-query implementation does not share the C128 prefix or expose raw prefix state. The inspected work does not implement this SM90 C128 prefix/state/tail specialization. This is a scoped search result, not a claim of novelty or an exhaustive duplicate-work guarantee.
AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and preparation of this PR description. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

The tested 8,192-token configuration completed long-context serving; this does not validate memory budgeting at 32k batched tokens or at higher concurrency. Multi-image requests, other head counts, other architectures, decode speed, and full model quality benchmarks are outside the measured claims. Exact output agreement is scoped to the tested Hopper implementation and pinned dependency/compiler versions.
Related work and duplicate check (2026-10-26) Query grouping is an existing optimization direction. [vLLM #48726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48726) includes structure-aware C128 query packing on SM100 alongside indexer optimizations. This change targets SM90, uses BF16 gathered KV, and preserves legacy FlashMLA arithmetic through explicit prefix-state continuation. [#63104](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63104) groups queries for FA4 sparse prefill with 16–64 local heads on SM100. [SGLang #32779](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32779) uses Triton sparse-query unions, including on SM90, rather than this native C128 continuation. [#59131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59131) reuses gathered KV across layers; [#41836](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41836) avoids BF16 gathering via a KV-cache path. This implementation retains gathering and shares KV within a query tile. [FlashMLA #170](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA/pull/170) changes producer scheduling; [FlashMLA #227](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA/pull/227) targets fused H64 attention on B200. The base already includes [#61615](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61615), enabling the existing small-head operation for V4.1. That per-query implementation does not share the C128 prefix or expose raw prefix state. The inspected work does not implement this SM90 C128 prefix/state/tail specialization. This is a scoped search result, not a claim of novelty or an exhaustive duplicate-work guarantee.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Compare shared-KV C128 prefill against padded-head FlashMLA on Hopper.
+
+Example:
+    .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_deepseek_v4_c128_prefill.py
+
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.ops.c128_prefill import c128_prefill_attention
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.flashmla import flash_mla_sparse_fwd
+
+
+def measure(context: int, query_len: int) -> dict:
+    num_heads = 8
+    compressed = context // 128
+    gather_len = min(context, query_len + 127)
+    q = torch.randn(query_len, 64, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    q[:, num_heads:] = 0
+    kv = torch.randn(
+        1, compressed + gather_len, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    sink = torch.randn(64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    candidate_out, reference_out = torch.empty_like(q), torch.empty_like(q)
+    seq_lens = torch.tensor([context], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    gather_lens = torch.tensor([gather_len], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    pos = torch.arange(context - query_len, context, device="cuda")
+    compressed_lens = (pos + 1) // 128
+    swa_lens = torch.minimum(pos + 1, torch.full_like(pos, 128))
+    lens = (compressed_lens + swa_lens).int()
+    columns = torch.arange(triton.cdiv(compressed + 128, 128) * 128, device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.where(
+        columns[None, :] < compressed_lens[:, None],
+        columns[None, :],
+        compressed
+        + pos[:, None]
+        - swa_lens[:, None]
+        + 1
+        + columns[None, :]
+        - compressed_lens[:, None]
+        - (context - gather_len),
+    )
+    indices = torch.where(columns[None, :] < lens[:, None], indices, -1).int()
+
+    def candidate():
+        c128_prefill_attention(
+            q,
+            kv,
+            sink,
+            candidate_out,
+            seq_lens,
+            gather_lens,
+            compressed,
+            512**-0.5,
+        )
+
+    def reference():
+        flash_mla_sparse_fwd(
+            q,
+            kv.view(-1, 1, 512),
+            indices[:, None, :],
+            512**-0.5,
+            attn_sink=sink,
+            topk_length=lens,
+            out=reference_out,
+        )
+
+    candidate()
+    reference()
+    candidate_bits = candidate_out[:, :num_heads].view(torch.int16)
+    reference_bits = reference_out[:, :num_heads].view(torch.int16)
+    assert torch.equal(candidate_bits, reference_bits)
+    # Also report both implementations' error against FP32 mathematics.
+    oracle_errors = {"candidate": 0.0, "reference": 0.0}
+    for row in sorted({0, 1, query_len // 2, query_len - 2, query_len - 1}):
+        if row < 0 or row >= query_len:
+            continue
+        keys = kv.view(-1, 512)[indices[row, : lens[row]].long()].float()
+        scores = q[row, :num_heads].float() @ keys.T * (512**-0.5)
+        normalizer = torch.logaddexp(scores.logsumexp(-1), sink[:num_heads])
+        oracle = torch.exp(scores - normalizer[:, None]) @ keys
+        for name, output in (
+            ("candidate", candidate_out),
+            ("reference", reference_out),
+        ):
+            oracle_errors[name] = max(
+                oracle_errors[name],
+                (output[row, :num_heads].float() - oracle).abs().max().item(),
+            )
+    reference_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(reference, warmup=100, rep=300)
+    candidate_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(candidate, warmup=100, rep=300)
+    return {
+        "context": context,
+        "num_heads": num_heads,
+        "query_len": query_len,
+        "reference_ms": reference_ms,
+        "candidate_ms": candidate_ms,
+        "speedup": reference_ms / candidate_ms,
+        "bitwise_mismatches": (candidate_bits != reference_bits).sum().item(),
+        "max_error_to_fp32": oracle_errors,
+        "max_error": (
+            candidate_out[:, :num_heads].float() - reference_out[:, :num_heads].float()
+        )
+        .abs()
+        .max()
+        .item(),
+    }
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--contexts", type=int, nargs="+", default=[8192, 131072, 1048576]
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--query-len", type=int, default=8192)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    torch.manual_seed(123)
+    for context in args.contexts:
+        print(
+            json.dumps(measure(context, min(args.query_len, context))),
+            flush=True,
+        )

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+#include "core/registration.h"
+#include "prefill.h"
+
+#include <cuda_runtime.h>
+#include <initializer_list>
+#include <torch/csrc/stable/accelerator.h>
+#include <torch/csrc/stable/library.h>
+#include <torch/csrc/stable/tensor.h>
+#include <torch/headeronly/core/ScalarType.h>
+#include <kerutils/supplemental/cuda_stream.h>
+
+using torch::headeronly::ScalarType;
+using torch::stable::Tensor;
+
+void c128_prefill(const Tensor& q, const Tensor& packed, const Tensor& kv,
+                  const Tensor& sink, const Tensor& lengths,
+                  const Tensor& seq_lens, const Tensor& gather_lens,
+                  Tensor& out, Tensor& raw_o, Tensor& raw_m, Tensor& raw_l,
+                  int64_t compressed_width, double scale) {
+  STD_TORCH_CHECK(q.dim() == 3 && q.size(1) == 64 && q.size(2) == 512,
+                  "C128 requires padded [tokens, 64, 512] queries");
+  STD_TORCH_CHECK(q.scalar_type() == ScalarType::BFloat16 &&
+                      packed.scalar_type() == ScalarType::BFloat16 &&
+                      kv.scalar_type() == ScalarType::BFloat16 &&
+                      out.scalar_type() == ScalarType::BFloat16,
+                  "C128 query, packed query, KV and output must be BF16");
+  STD_TORCH_CHECK(q.stride(1) == 512 && q.stride(2) == 1 &&
+                      out.sizes() == q.sizes() && out.stride(1) == 512 &&
+                      out.stride(2) == 1,
+                  "invalid C128 query/output layout");
+  int64_t padded = ((q.size(0) + 7) / 8) * 8;
+  STD_TORCH_CHECK(
+      packed.numel() == padded * 8 * 512 && packed.is_contiguous() &&
+          raw_o.numel() == padded * 8 * 512 && raw_o.is_contiguous() &&
+          raw_m.numel() == padded * 8 && raw_m.is_contiguous() &&
+          raw_l.numel() == padded * 8 * 8 && raw_l.is_contiguous(),
+      "invalid C128 workspace");
+  STD_TORCH_CHECK(raw_o.scalar_type() == ScalarType::Float &&
+                      raw_m.scalar_type() == ScalarType::Float &&
+                      raw_l.scalar_type() == ScalarType::Float &&
+                      sink.scalar_type() == ScalarType::Float &&
+                      sink.numel() >= 8 && sink.is_contiguous(),
+                  "invalid C128 floating-point buffers");
+  STD_TORCH_CHECK(lengths.numel() == padded / 8 && lengths.is_contiguous() &&
+                      lengths.scalar_type() == ScalarType::Int &&
+                      seq_lens.numel() == 1 && gather_lens.numel() == 1 &&
+                      seq_lens.scalar_type() == ScalarType::Int &&
+                      gather_lens.scalar_type() == ScalarType::Int,
+                  "invalid C128 metadata");
+  STD_TORCH_CHECK(kv.dim() == 3 && kv.size(0) == 1 && kv.size(2) == 512 &&
+                      kv.stride(1) == 512 && kv.stride(2) == 1 &&
+                      compressed_width >= 0 && compressed_width <= kv.size(1),
+                  "invalid C128 KV layout");
+  for (const Tensor* t : std::initializer_list<const Tensor*>{
+           &q, &packed, &kv, &sink, &lengths, &seq_lens, &gather_lens, &out,
+           &raw_o, &raw_m, &raw_l}) {
+    STD_TORCH_CHECK(t->device().is_cuda() && t->device() == q.device(),
+                    "all C128 tensors must be on the same CUDA device");
+  }
+  STD_TORCH_CHECK(q.size(0) <= INT32_MAX && q.stride(0) <= INT32_MAX &&
+                      out.stride(0) <= INT32_MAX && kv.size(1) <= INT32_MAX &&
+                      q.size(0) * q.stride(0) <= INT32_MAX &&
+                      q.size(0) * out.stride(0) <= INT32_MAX,
+                  "C128 dimensions exceed int32");
+  torch::stable::accelerator::DeviceGuard guard(q.get_device_index());
+  c128_run(q.data_ptr(), packed.data_ptr(), kv.data_ptr(), sink.data_ptr(),
+           lengths.data_ptr(), out.mutable_data_ptr(), raw_o.mutable_data_ptr(),
+           raw_m.mutable_data_ptr(), raw_l.mutable_data_ptr(),
+           seq_lens.data_ptr(), gather_lens.data_ptr(), q.size(0), kv.size(1),
+           compressed_width, q.stride(0), out.stride(0),
+           static_cast<float>(scale), kerutils::get_current_cuda_stream(q));
+}
+
+STABLE_TORCH_LIBRARY(_c128_C, m) {
+  m.def(
+      "prefill(Tensor q, Tensor packed, Tensor kv, Tensor sink, Tensor "
+      "lengths, "
+      "Tensor seq_lens, Tensor gather_lens, Tensor(a!) out, Tensor(b!) raw_o, "
+      "Tensor(c!) raw_m, Tensor(d!) raw_l, int compressed_width, float scale) "
+      "-> ()");
+}
+
+STABLE_TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL(_c128_C, CUDA, m) {
+  m.impl("prefill", TORCH_BOX(&c128_prefill));
+}
+
+REGISTER_EXTENSION(_c128_C)

 --8<-- "gen:table-mla-decode"
 
+### DeepSeek V4 C128 Prefill on Hopper
+
+The `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` backend automatically uses the optional `_c128_C`
+extension for eligible DeepSeek V4 text prefills on Hopper (H100/H200). Source
+builds include this target for supported architectures; precompiled installations
+need to build it separately. No additional serving flag is required. Without
+the extension, prefill uses the existing FlashMLA path.
+
+The optimization shares compressed KV across eight queries with eight local
+heads. It requires BF16 queries, a 128-token sliding window, at least 512
+compressed KV rows (65,536 context tokens), at least 4,096 query tokens, and one
+prefill request in the workspace group. Image visibility, batch invariant
+execution, other shapes, and decode use the existing path. Workspace grouping
+can therefore affect whether concurrent prefills use the optimization.
+
+The shared-prefix and per-query-tail kernels preserve the pinned FlashMLA
+accumulation and rounding order using unnormalized FP32 intermediate state.
+The staging buffers use approximately 194 MiB for 8,192 query tokens. Bitwise
+compatibility applies to the tested Hopper implementation, not to the whole
+model across different batches or compiler/dependency versions.
+
 ### DeepSeek V4 Decode Backends
 
 DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA uses its own decode backends, selected via

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""C128 prefill with shared compressed KV across adjacent query tokens."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+try:
+    import vllm._c128_C  # noqa: F401
+
+    HAS_NATIVE_C128 = True
+except ImportError:
+    HAS_NATIVE_C128 = False
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _pack_c128_queries(q, packed, lengths, seq_len, stride: tl.constexpr, n):
+    token = tl.program_id(0)
+    index = tl.arange(0, 4096)
+    values = tl.load(q + token * stride + index, token < n, other=0)
+    tl.store(packed + token * 4096 + index, values)
+    if token % 8 == 0:
+        seq = tl.load(seq_len)
+        common = ((seq - n + token + 1) // 128) // 128 * 128
+        tl.store(lengths + token // 8, common)
+
+
+def c128_prefill_attention(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    kv: torch.Tensor,
+    attn_sink: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    gather_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    compressed_width: int,
+    scale: float,
+) -> None:
+    """Attend to the causal compressed prefix and 128-token sliding window.
+
+    Pack eight queries with eight active heads into each shared-prefix tile.
+    Save unnormalized FP32 state before continuing each query's tail in CUDA,
+    preserving the pinned Hopper FlashMLA accumulation and rounding order.
+    The caller selects supported text prefills and otherwise uses FlashMLA.
+
+    Args:
+        q: BF16 queries, [tokens, 64, 512], with eight active heads.
+        kv: Gathered BF16 KV, [1, workspace_width, 512]. The compressed
+            prefix occupies [0, compressed_width), followed by gathered SWA KV.
+        attn_sink: FP32 sink logits, at least eight elements.
+        out: Output buffer with the same layout as q; writes the active heads.
+        seq_lens: Sequence lengths including the current query tokens.
+        gather_lens: Number of uncompressed KV rows gathered per request.
+        compressed_width: Offset of the uncompressed region in each KV row.
+        scale: Query-key softmax scale.
+
+    """
+    assert HAS_NATIVE_C128, "C128 prefill requires the native _c128_C extension"
+    # Q packing runs before the C++ entry point validates the other tensors.
+    assert q.is_cuda and seq_lens.device == q.device and seq_lens.numel() == 1
+    assert q.ndim == 3 and q.shape[1:] == (64, 512)
+    assert q.stride(1) == 512 and q.stride(2) == 1
+    if q.shape[0] == 0:
+        return
+    num_tokens = q.shape[0]
+    padded_tokens = triton.cdiv(num_tokens, 8) * 8
+    packed_q = torch.empty((padded_tokens, 8, 512), device=q.device, dtype=q.dtype)
+    raw_o = torch.empty((padded_tokens, 8, 512), device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    raw_m = torch.empty((padded_tokens, 8), device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    raw_l = torch.empty((padded_tokens, 8, 2, 4), device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    lengths = torch.empty((padded_tokens // 8,), device=q.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    _pack_c128_queries[(padded_tokens,)](
+        q, packed_q, lengths, seq_lens, q.stride(0), num_tokens, num_warps=4
+    )
+    torch.ops._c128_C.prefill(
+        q,
+        packed_q,
+        kv,
+        attn_sink,
+        lengths,
+        seq_lens,
+        gather_lens,
+        out,
+        raw_o,
+        raw_m,
+        raw_l,
+        compressed_width,
+        scale * 1.4426950216293335,
+    )
